battle.name: 高熲攻陳之戰
battle.brief: 開皇元年隋文帝代周建國，開皇八年冬下詔伐陳，開皇九年正月大軍分道渡江，采石、廣陵兩路合圍建康，陳朝覆亡。卡面羅馬標槍並未隨軍而至，它所代表的重投槍類在長江戰場上對應的仍是弩、弓與長柄槍；真正決戰的是楊素的巨艦火攻與韓擒虎五百人夜渡采石。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是開皇元年（581）二月受北周恭帝禪位而立的隋朝，和據江南的南朝陳。隋朝以關隴軍事集團為骨幹，地方上由柱國、將軍、總管、刺史層層承包的軍府系統承載兵役；朝廷則以尚書省出令、兵部調將、戶部調糧，三者互相牽制。滅陳的指揮分四路鋪開：行軍元帥楊廣總淮南方向，楊俊總山南方向，楊素總上游舟師，另有上柱國王韶率兵自漢中沿沔水東下，與山南一路策應；先鋒與戰線上的實際衝鋒由賀若弼、韓擒虎、盧辨等將領分擔，每路配將作、監軍、參軍，糧秣按州郡戶口就地徵發。陳朝那邊，朝廷以都督諸軍事掌兵、州刺史掌地，陳後主陳叔寶坐鎮建康，蕭摩訶、陳僧誼、歐陽頠、袁君正分守姑孰、采石、江陵一線；江上以五牙大艦、蒙衝、艨艟組成龐大舟師，岸防則倚樓車、雲梯、撞車。這是一場以長江天塹為核心的南北對峙，一方靠水軍與糧道縱深，一方靠既有城池與上游屏障。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Sui dynasty, founded in the second month of 581 when Emperor Wen Yang Jian accepted the abdication of the Zhou emperor Gong, and the Southern Chen dynasty holding the Jiangnan region. The Sui state was built on the military clans of the Guanzhong region; at the local level its army was carried by a hierarchy of command posts headed by pillar lords, generals, regional commanders and prefectural governors, while at the centre the Department of State Affairs issued the orders, the Ministry of War moved the commanders and the Ministry of Revenue moved the grain, each checking the others. The command for the conquest of Chen was laid out in four columns: the marshal Yang Guang took the Huai River sector, Yang Jun the mountainous south, Yang Su the river fleet on the upper reaches, and the pillar lord Wang Shao marched down the Han River from Hanzhong to support the southern column. The actual shock work on the battle line was handed to leaders such as He Ruobi, Han Qinhu and Lu Bian, each column equipped with directors of works, inspectors and staff officers, and grain was levied in place from the households of each prefecture. On the Chen side the state rested on regional commanders holding military authority and governors holding territory: the last Chen emperor, Chen Shubao, sat in the capital Jiankang, while Xiao Mohe, Chen Sengyi, Ouyang Wei and Yuan Junzheng were posted to guard Gutu, Caishi and Jiangling. On the river a huge fleet of five-tooth great ships, ram-boats and war junks carried the river defence, while towers, siege ladders and battering rams covered the banks. This was a confrontation pivoting on the natural moat of the Yangtze: one side relied on its fleet and the depth of its supply lines, the other on existing cities and the upstream screen.
people: 「高熲」是戰役名號所繫之人。他是北周柱國，與宇文護、宇文憲、獨孤信並列，主持北周中後期西線與南線的軍務，卒於周宣帝在位年間；隋文帝受禪之後對北周舊柱國及其子弟仍加優容，因此「高熲」這個名字在隋初的敘述裡常被繫在滅陳這類大業上。不過現存史籍（《隋書·高祖紀》《楊素傳》《資治通鑑》卷一百七十九、一百八十）並沒有留下他親自領兵攻陳的獨立戰報，此役的實際執行者是另一批人。楊堅以「混一江南」為既定方針，開皇八年十月下詔伐陳，戰時坐鎮長安，統籌四方兵馬與糧道。楊廣以淮南行省尚書令總督東線，開皇九年正月預聞渡江之役。楊素領上游主力，造五牙大艦與黃龍艦，順流直取建康；楊俊自襄陽趨江陵，王韶循沔水東下。賀若弼自廣陵濟江，是西路最銳的突破手；韓擒虎以五百人夜渡采石，攻入姑孰，一舉撕開江防。陳朝一端，陳後主臨機決斷遲緩，蕭摩訶坐鎮姑孰，是陳最倚重的猛將；陳僧誼守采石，歐陽頠拒江陵。建康城破之日，陳後主與張麗華、孔貴嬪自景陽殿井中被拖出，陳氏政權隨之崩解。
peopleEn: Gao Cu is the name the war is filed under. He was a pillar lord of the Northern Zhou, ranked alongside Yuwen Hu, Yuwen Xian and Dugu Xin, and he directed the western and southern operations of the Zhou in its later years; he died while Emperor Xuan of Zhou was still on the throne. After accepting the abdication in 581, Sui Wen treated the old pillar lords and their sons with generosity, and so Gao Cu's name in Sui-era narrative was often tied to great undertakings such as the conquest of Chen. The surviving records, however, contain no separate battle report of his leading troops against Chen; the men who actually executed the war were others. Yang Jian took the unification of the south as settled policy, issued the edict to attack Chen in the tenth month of 588, and remained at Chang'an to direct the four columns and the supply lines. Yang Guang, as director of the Huai River circuit, took charge of the eastern column and was present at the crossing in the first month of 589. Yang Su led the main force on the upper river, building the five-tooth great ships and the yellow-dragon ships to drift straight down towards Jiankang; Yang Jun moved from Xiangyang against Jiangling, and Wang Shao came down the Mian River. He Ruobi crossed from Guangling and was the sharpest arm of the western thrust, while Han Qinhu took five hundred men across at night at Caishi, entered Gutu and tore open the river line in a single stroke. On the Chen side, the last emperor hesitated in his decisions; Xiao Mohe, posted at Gutu, was the most trusted of Chen's fighting commanders, Chen Sengyi held Caishi and Ouyang Wei held Jiangling. On the day the capital fell, Chen Shubao, together with Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei, was dragged out of the well in the Jingyang Hall, and the Chen government came apart with him.
kits: 卡面兵器是羅馬標槍（Pilum），但公元六世紀末的長江戰場上並無羅馬裝備。標槍是古典地中海世界的重投槍代表：槍桿中空，以竹管貼木芯製成，前端套鐵矛頭，卡面所刻的就是那截半米左右的槍桿，接上矛頭之後全槍長度接近兩米；軍團改編後每兵攜帶兩支，投擲距離約二三十米。它的關鍵在於槍桿撞上盾牌或鎧甲後會折斷，敵人無法拔出再用，羅馬人索性把折斷的標槍插在防線前當作障礙，阻擋敵騎衝陣。本役中與標槍對應的，是中國自己的投射體系：弩（張弩、蹶張弩）、弓，以及步軍手中的長柄槍、矛、槊與投槍；攻城方向用雲梯、撞車、望樓與堞；水戰方面，楊素的舟師主力是五牙大艦與黃龍艦，船上備拍車以拍擊敵舷，隋軍另備火炬，遇陳軍蒙衝即投擲焚燒，陳軍則在沿江鑄鐵鎖橫斷水面阻擋隋船，隋軍遣小船載火炬潛近熔斷鐵鎖，隨後以大艦硬撞。兩套體系的共通點很清楚：靠重投射物加近身撞擊取勝，而不是靠遠程火力。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman pilum, but no Roman equipment stood on the Yangtze fighting ground in the late sixth century. The pilum was the heavy javelin of the classical Mediterranean: a hollow shaft built from a bamboo tube backed with a wooden core, capped by an iron shank, the half-metre hollow section being exactly what the card depicts, so that with the shank fitted the whole weapon came close to two metres. After the legionary reform each soldier carried two of them and threw them from twenty to thirty metres. The point of the design was that the hollow shaft snapped when it struck a shield or a cuirass, so the enemy could not pull it out and reuse it; the Romans accordingly stuck their broken shafts in front of the line as an obstacle against cavalry. What corresponds to the pilum in this war is the Chinese system of missiles: the crossbow, both the tension bow and the foot-powered crossbow, the ordinary bow, and the long-handled spear, the ji and the shao carried by the infantry, together with javelins. For siege work the armies used scaling ladders, battering rams, watch towers and parapets. On the water Yang Su's fleet leaned on the five-tooth great ships and the yellow-dragon ships, with beating devices to smash the sides of enemy hulls, while the Sui carried torches to set the Chen ram-boats alight on sight; the Chen in turn cast iron chains across the river to bar the Sui ships, and Sui men in small boats crept up with torches to melt the chains before the heavy hulls drove through. The common denominator of both systems is clear: massed missiles followed by close physical impact, not long-range firepower.
tactics: 開皇八年十月下詔之後，隋軍不急於求戰，先把四路兵力的時間表對齊：楊素的舟師要順流千里，必須先把船造好、把糧運到永安；楊廣、楊俊兩路則等江面北風與水位配合。開皇八年十二月，楊素自永安放船，黃龍、五牙大艦在前，連接成片，帆檣蔽江；上游陳軍在江州一帶鑄鐵鎖橫江，隋軍派小船載火炬潛近熔鎖，主力隨即以大艦硬撞。開皇九年正月，隋軍分道渡江：賀若弼自廣陵濟，韓擒虎率五百人夜渡采石，采石的水軍與姑孰的蕭摩訶部先後崩潰，隋軍因而下游無阻，兩路很快合圍建康。攻城不靠強攻：隋文帝事前已密遣使者入城招降陳方將領，城內人心浮動，守軍屢見崩解，隋軍遂得長驅入城。掩護與牽制方面，楊素以連鎖大艦結陣前進吸引陳軍主力，東西兩線再以賀若弼、韓擒虎的快速突破撕開缺口。補給線靠益州、永安的糧船順流北上，再轉運到各軍，逐日按計劃下達。陳軍的戰術是死守天塹：以舟師封江口、以城池拒敵、靠上游屏障遲滯隋軍，結果是處處得守而處處失守，關鍵時刻無人能把五六處戰線上的兵合到一處。
tacticsEn: After the edict of the tenth month of 588 the Sui did not rush into battle; they first aligned the timetables of the four columns. Yang Su's fleet had to drift a thousand li down the river, so the ships had to be built and the grain moved to Yong'an first, while the columns of Yang Guang and Yang Jun waited for the northerly winds and the water level. In the twelfth month of 588 Yang Su launched his fleet from Yong'an, the yellow-dragon and five-tooth great ships leading and the hulls joined up into a single spread with sails and masts covering the river. The Chen had cast iron chains across the water around Jiangzhou to bar the way; Sui men in small boats with torches crept up and melted the chains, and the main fleet immediately drove through with its heavy hulls. In the first month of 589 the Sui crossed in several columns: He Ruobi from Guangling, and Han Qinhu with five hundred men across at night at Caishi. The Chen fleet at Caishi broke first, the troops of Xiao Mohe at Gutu followed, and with the lower river open the two Sui columns closed on Jiankang. The city was not stormed: Sui Wen had already sent secret emissaries into it to sound out the Chen commanders, the garrison was unsettled, the defenders kept breaking, and the Sui troops walked into the city. For cover and deception Yang Su advanced with his linked great ships to draw the main weight of the Chen army, while the eastern and western columns made fast breaches with the sudden thrusts of He Ruobi and Han Qinhu. Supply ran on grain boats from Yizhou and Yong'an drifting north with the current and then being transferred to each column day by day according to plan. The Chen plan was to hold the natural barrier: sealing the river mouths with the fleet, refusing the assault from the cities, and using the upstream screen to slow the Sui down. The result was a defence that held everywhere and lost everywhere, because at the critical moment nobody could bring the troops of five or six separate fronts together.
data: 開皇元年（581）二月，隋文帝受周恭帝禪位，改元開皇，本條目所繫的年份即此建國之年，實際出兵則在開皇八年冬。開皇八年（588）十月下詔伐陳，十二月主力自永安發船，開皇九年（589）正月渡江。兵力規模諸書所記不一，或稱發兵五十餘萬，或稱六十餘萬；若連同運糧、造船的役夫一併計算，總數當遠高於此。隋軍投入的戰船，楊素一路即有兵船千餘艘、甲士十餘萬，隨軍糧米數十萬石。五牙大艦船身高十餘丈，上起層樓，可容數百人；黃龍艦同類，兩者前後相接，帆檣蔽江。韓擒虎的夜渡先鋒只有五百人，取的是人少、夜靜、敵軍酣睡三個條件。采石距建康不足百里，沿江兩處渡口相隔不過數日行程，隋軍自渡江到建康城陷不過旬日。陳方江上舟師連綴，禁軍精銳多集中於建康與京口，州郡兵力分散各守一線。開皇九年五月，陳湘州刺史蕭岩以湘州降隋；陳將王琳起兵反隋，到開皇十一年才被平定，江南全部歸附因而拖了近三年。史籍界線也須說明：本條目年份是編年起點，與戰役實際執行的歲月相去約八年，數字只取《隋書》與《資治通鑑》可以互證者。
dataEn: In the second month of 581 Sui Wen received the abdication of the Zhou emperor Gong and changed the era to Kaihuang; the year this entry is filed under is that founding year, while the campaign itself was fought in the winter of 588. The edict to attack Chen went out in the tenth month of 588, the main fleet left Yong'an in the twelfth month, and the crossing was made in the first month of 589. The records differ on the size of the army, some giving more than five hundred thousand men, others more than six hundred thousand; counting the porters who moved grain and built the ships, the total must have been far higher. On Yang Su's column alone the Sui put more than a thousand warships to sea with over a hundred thousand armoured men and several hundred thousand measures of grain. The five-tooth great ship stood more than ten zhang high, carried storeys above its deck and held several hundred men; the yellow-dragon ship was of the same kind, and the two kinds were lashed together in line with sails and masts covering the river. The night crossing under Han Qinhu used only five hundred men, relying on three conditions: few men, a dark night and an enemy asleep. Caishi lies less than a hundred li from Jiankang, and the two crossing points on the river were a few days' march apart, so between the crossing and the fall of Jiankang no more than ten days passed. The Chen fleet was strung out along the river, with the best of the palace troops concentrated at Jiankang and Jingkou and the prefectural forces scattered to hold separate lines. In the fifth month of 589 Xiao Yan, the Chen governor of Xiangzhou, surrendered that province; the Chen general Wang Lin rose in revolt and was not put down until 591, so the submission of the south dragged on for nearly three years. The limit of the record should be stated as well: the year of this entry is the starting point of the chronicle, roughly eight years before the war was actually fought, and the figures here are only those on which the Suishu and the Zizhi Tongjian agree.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。表層是南朝陳的失政：陳後主陳叔寶在位後期怠於政事，寵信張麗華、孔貴嬌一類嬪御，大興佛寺與宮室工程，賦役加重，江南方鎮隨之離心；北方大軍一壓到江邊，陳朝既無可獨當一面的統帥，也無可支撐長期抵抗的財力。中間層是北周留下的舊賬：北周自宇文護到宇文憲多次南下攻陳，六十年代華州失利、七十年代初建康之役無功而返，滅陳的構想在關隴集團裡醞釀了半個世紀，高熲這類柱國正是在這條線上辦軍務、籌糧草；隋承周制，天然承下這份未竟的清單。第三層是隋朝自身的政治需要：開皇元年楊堅代周建隋，北方尚有尉遲迥、宇文賢等舊勢力未平，宇文賢據鄴城，直到當年十月才被平定；新朝必須先在北方站穩，再以一場壓倒性的勝利證明正統，坐實「混一」的國策。最實際的一層是後勤：開皇年間隋朝在益州、永安一線造船蓄糧，為順流而下的主力備好艦船與糧秣；楊廣上表指出陳的糧食多從交州沿江運到建康，水路數千里，隋朝則把江南之米經運河南運京師，既補自身軍食，也意在斷陳的糧道。戰爭名號裡「高熲」一語，現存史料沒有留下他領兵攻陳的獨立戰報，這條戰記的記載有限，但可以確定的是：它是北周舊人主導的滅陳方略，在隋朝開國之後被全面執行。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause behind the war. The surface layer is the misgovernment of the Southern Chen: in the later years of his reign the last Chen emperor, Chen Shubao, neglected government, favoured consorts such as Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei, lavished on Buddhist temples and palace works, and increased the burden of service and tax, so that the regional commanders of the south grew restive. Once a northern army reached the river, the Chen had neither a commander who could hold the field on his own nor the financial means to sustain a long resistance. The middle layer is an old account inherited from the Northern Zhou: from Yuwen Hu to Yuwen Xian the Zhou had marched south against Chen again and again, losing at Huazhou in the 560s and returning empty-handed from the campaign against Jiankang in the early 570s. The idea of destroying Chen had been fermenting in the Guanzhong group for half a century, and men such as Gao Cu ran the staff work and the logistics on that line; the Sui inherited the Zhou institutions and therefore inherited this unfinished list. The third layer is the political need of the new Sui state: when Yang Jian replaced the Zhou in 581, old northern powers such as Yuwen Jiong and Yuwen Xian were still in the field, and Yuwen Xian held Ye until that very October; the new dynasty had to first hold its ground in the north and then prove its legitimacy with one overwhelming victory, fixing the policy of unification in place. The most practical layer is logistics: through the Kaihuang years the Sui built ships and stored grain on the Yizhou and Yong'an line so that the main force coming down the river would have hulls and provisions waiting for it. Yang Guang reported to the throne that Chen's grain came largely from Jiaozhi up the river to Jiankang, a water route of several thousand li, while the Sui moved the rice of the south through the canal to the northern capital, feeding its own armies and at the same time aiming at Chen's supply line. As for the name Gao Cu carried by this war, the surviving records contain no separate report of his leading troops against Chen; the record of this campaign is thin, but what can be fixed is this: it was the scheme for destroying Chen drawn up by the old men of the Northern Zhou, and it was carried out in full once the Sui had taken the throne.
impact: 第一層後果是國家的形狀變了。南北分裂近三百年，到開皇九年一併結束，隋朝拿到陳的全部版圖，疆域、水利、戶口與賦稅一併擴大，此後二十年的開皇之治有了統一的地盤作為前提。第二層是制度的定型：開皇律令、州縣與戶籍整理、三省六部與府兵制的組合在滅陳之後陸續落地，江南新附之地又要另行安撫，隋朝對南方暫用舊法、漸改新制，整套國家機器自此在南北兩套財政與軍制之間尋找平衡。第三層是軍事能力的轉向：統一之後，隋朝能把關隴、中原與江南的資源一起編成大軍，幾年後便有能力兩征高句麗，把國力重心推向東北；統一既是新的力量來源，也是新的消耗方向。第四層是文獻與文藝的流動：陳氏宗室與南朝文人北遷，庾信、陳後主的作品進入北方文壇，隋初收陳圖籍、校定群書，長安的藏書與洛陽的刻本由此擴充；南朝樂府與宮廷詩的聲律也隨文人北上而為唐人承繼。第五層是水戰技術的積累：巨艦衝撞、火炬焚舟、鐵鎖橫江與夜渡奇襲這一整套長江經驗，此後長期留在隋唐水軍的記憶裡，成為唐初水軍訓練與水戰教材的內容。
impactEn: The first consequence was a change in the shape of the state. Nearly three centuries of division between north and south ended at once in 589, and the Sui took over the whole territory of Chen; frontier, waterworks, households and taxes all grew together, and the two decades of the Kaihuang settlement that followed rested on a unified ground. The second was the fixing of institutions: the Kaihuang code, the prefectures and counties with the re-registration of households, the three departments and six ministries, and the fubing military system all settled into place after the conquest, while the newly attached south needed its own handling, the Sui keeping old usages there for a time and moving gradually to the new ones, so that the whole machinery of state searched for a balance between two sets of fiscal and military arrangements, one northern and one southern. The third was a turn in military capacity: once unified, the Sui could marshal the resources of Guanzhong, the central plain and the south into a single great army, and within a few years it was able to mount two campaigns against Goguryeo and to push the weight of the empire towards the northeast. Unification was both a new source of strength and a new direction of expenditure. The fourth was the movement of texts and letters: the Chen royal clan and the writers of the south moved north, the work of Yu Xin and of the last Chen emperor entered the literary life of the north, and at the beginning of the Sui the confiscation of Chen's books and the collation of the collections enlarged both the holdings of Chang'an and the block-printing of Luoyang; the tonal techniques of the southern yuefu and court verse travelled north with their authors and were taken up by the Tang. The fifth was the accumulation of river-war technique: ramming great hulls, burning with torches, chaining the river and the surprise crossing by night stayed in the memory of Sui and Tang river armies, and became material for the training drills and river-war manuals of the early Tang.
result: 開皇九年正月，隋軍主力自采石、廣陵一線渡江，采石水軍先潰，姑孰蕭摩訶部隨即瓦解，賀若弼占京口，兩路會於建康城下。城破之日，陳後主陳叔寶與張麗華、孔貴嬪自景陽殿井中被拖出，禁軍與州兵群龍無首，淮北諸州郡相繼歸附，陳朝滅亡，隋朝得江南之地，晉王楊廣以淮南行省尚書令領有戰功。陳將蕭摩訶、陳僧誼等先後歸降，姓名改列隋朝將籍，據《隋書》，蕭摩訶更隨楊廣東征高句麗，兵敗後才被免官。江南餘部沒有立刻平靜：陳湘州刺史蕭岩據湘州拒守，到開皇九年五月才以全州降隋；陳將王琳以陳室舊臣的名義起兵，在琅琊、鄱陽一帶活動，直到開皇十一年才被平定，江南的歸附因此拖了將近三年。論功行賞之後，隋軍各路凱旋北還，隋文帝把陳後主封為鄭王，連同宗室遷於洛陽，江南的賦役一度減免，以收人心。這一役的最終結果可以這樣概括：以一次壓倒性的渡江攻勢，在數旬之內拆掉一個延續近三百年的王朝，而陳朝的君主與將領大都保住了性命，敗亡的只是政權本身。
resultEn: In the first month of 589 the main Sui force crossed the river at the line of Caishi and Guangling. The Chen fleet at Caishi broke first, the troops of Xiao Mohe at Gutu fell apart next, He Ruobi occupied Jingkou, and the two columns met beneath Jiankang. On the day the city fell, Chen Shubao, with Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei, was dragged out of the well in the Jingyang Hall; the palace guards and the prefectural troops lost all command, the prefectures north of the Huai submitted in turn, the Chen dynasty was destroyed and the Sui took the southern country, with the Prince of Jin Yang Guang carrying the credit as director of the Huai River circuit. Chen commanders such as Xiao Mohe and Chen Sengyi surrendered in turn and their names passed into the Sui registers of commanders; according to the Suishu, Xiao Mohe later marched east with Yang Guang against Goguryeo and was only dismissed after the defeat. The south did not settle at once. Xiao Yan, the Chen governor of Xiangzhou, held out and surrendered that province only in the fifth month of 589; the Chen general Wang Lin rose in the name of the old Chen house and moved about Langya and Poyang, and was not put down until 591, so the submission of the south dragged on for nearly three years. After the rewards were counted the Sui columns returned north in triumph. Sui Wen made the last Chen emperor Prince of Zheng and moved him and the rest of the clan to Luoyang, and the taxes and levies of the south were reduced for a time to win hearts. The final result can be put in one sentence: a single overwhelming crossing of the river destroyed in a few weeks a dynasty that had run for nearly three centuries, while the Chen emperor and most of his commanders kept their lives, and what fell was the regime alone.
